title: Heuristic fallback playbook and rollback writeup - tokenizer drift + config skew
body:
Summary:

On 2024-02-19 we observed a canary degradation during a scheduled rollout of model variant svc-gamma-v2. The failure mode was a mix of elevated decode errors and silent truncations in streamed responses originating from canary instances only. The symptoms appeared 7 minutes after canary traffic started to ramp and affected 2 of 6 canary hosts. Latency p95 stayed nominal for the first 3 minutes then spiked alongside decode_error_rate.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture the incident timeline and immediate mitigations.
- Capture quick runbook steps for on-call to revert similar incidents faster.
- Propose persistent fixes (preflight checks, coupling artifact bundles, rollout heuristics).

Severity: P1 (partial production degradation contained to canaries, risk of broader rollout if unchecked).

Brief technical summary (root cause hypothesis):
- A tokenizer vocabulary patch (vocab-merge-2024-02-18) was published as a separate artifact and not bundled atomically with model weights.
- The deployment orchestration applied the new weight shards (svc-gamma-v2) to canaries before a synchronous update of tokenizer artifacts due to a race in artifact replication (manifest replication lag + orchestration no-op ordering).
- Some weight shards expected a shifted token ID mapping (new offsets). When older tokenizer vocab was still active on the host, decode produced invalid token IDs, leading to decode errors and truncated streaming.
- Manifest checksum replication lag and a heuristics threshold in the rollout controller permitted a partial apply when 2 canary nodes reported manifest mismatch but rollout continued.

Metrics observed (post-detection):
- decode_error_rate: baseline ~0.001% -> spike to 2.7% on affected canaries
- stream_truncation_count: +430 in 10m window compared to baseline
- p95 latency (inference): +120ms on affected hosts
- kv_cache_miss_rate: small uptick (+0.4%) (likely unrelated but noted)

Timeline (UTC):
- 2024-02-19 02:13:00 - canary rollout started (6 hosts, 10% traffic each).
- 2024-02-19 02:19:10 - automated canary health check: subtle increase in partial-decode metric; anomaly threshold not yet crossed.
- 2024-02-19 02:20:45 - alerts: decode_error_rate alert fired for host canary-2 and canary-5. SRE on-call paged.
- 2024-02-19 02:23:12 - on-call ran quick canary query: logs show token id mismatch entries (LOG: token id 50212 not in vocabulary mapping) in two hosts.
- 2024-02-19 02:25:00 - performed scoped traffic isolation to route traffic away from canary-2 and canary-5.
- 2024-02-19 02:27:30 - operator executed rollback command for svc-gamma-v2 on canaries (see commands below).
- 2024-02-19 02:30:00 - decode_error_rate returning to baseline; canary hosts healthy on previous model.
- 2024-02-19 02:58:00 - post-incident blameless review scheduled; artifact checks performed.

Immediate mitigation steps executed (what worked):
1) Traffic isolation: moved weighted traffic away from affected canaries via rollout controller quick-evict. This prevented broader user impact.
2) Canary rollback: rolled canaries back to svc-gamma-v1 (previous stable) using rollback CLI.
3) Temporary hold: paused global rollout and blocked auto-promote triggers until root-cause analysis.
4) Manual artifact re-sync: forced tokenizer artifact re-replication to the affected region and validated checksums.

Commands / snippets used during on-call (examples):
- Check canary health: redwoodctl rollout status svc-gamma --canaries
- Isolate host: redwoodctl host cordon canary-2 --reason "decode-errors"
- Rollback canary: redwoodctl rollout revert svc-gamma --to-version svc-gamma-v1 --scope canaries
- Force artifact pull and validate checksums: redwoodctl artifact fetch tokenizer:vocab-20240218 --validate-sha256
- Quick log query: logs query --filter "service:svc-gamma AND (decode_error OR token-id-mismatch)" --since 15m

Root cause analysis (deeper):
- Artifact decoupling: tokenizer vocab was published to object storage with eventual replication to regional caches. The rollout controller treated tokenizer and weights as independent artifacts and did not enforce an atomic bundle or version pin.
- Manifest ordering bug: the rollout controller uses a priority queue that favored weight shard application before tokenizer artifact availability if weight shard health checks passed. This is a latent bug in orchestration heuristics introduced when we added parallel artifact streaming optimization.
- Health check sensitivity: the canary health checks rely primarily on request success rate and latency. They did not include explicit tokenization validation (decode/round-trip tests), making the anomaly slow to cross the alerting threshold.

Why only subset of canaries?
- Replication lag: regionally, two canaries were served from a cache node that had not yet pulled the latest tokenizer blob. A small timing window allowed weights to apply there first.
- Non-deterministic ordering exposed the race due to parallel artifact streaming.

Immediate follow-ups (owners and ETA):
- Ensure rollout controller treats model bundle artifacts atomically (weights + tokenizer + config): owner Ethan Zhao, ETA 2024-03-15.
- Add preflight pre-deploy check: validate tokenizer hash vs model expected vocab-sha256 for every target host before weight apply: owner Marta Ruiz, ETA 2024-03-01 (high priority).
- Expand canary health checks to include a lightweight decode round-trip test (example prompt -> token sequence -> decode -> assert no unknown token ids): owner Daniel Kim, ETA 2024-03-08.
- Improve alerting thresholds for decode_error_rate and add per-host aggregation to reduce alert fatigue: owner Aisha Malik, ETA 2024-03-05.
- Postmortem doc and runbook update (this file): owner Aisha Malik, ETA 2024-03-04.

Longer-term mitigations (policy and infra):
- Atomic model bundles: modify artifact registry to require bundle manifests; disallow independent promotion unless explicit compatibility flag present.
- Rollout controller hardening: change priority policy to ensure tokenizer/config artifacts fully replicated and validated on a host before weights are applied.
- Preflight simulator: create a preflight harness that simulates a few deterministic tokenization/decoding sequences on target hosts prior to traffic routing.
- Replication telemetry: add alerting for manifest replication lag (object storage -> regional cache) exceeding X seconds (owner infra team).

Runbook (quick playbook for on-call when decode/tokenizer anomalies detected):
1) Confirm alert: identify hosts and check decode_error_rate per-host, stream_truncation_count.
2) Check artifact versions on affected hosts: redwoodctl host describe <host> --artifacts. Look for tokenizer:vocab-*.
3) If tokenizer version mismatch: (a) cordon host, (b) force artifact pull and validate checksums, (c) if artifacts fail to sync, rollback weights on host.
4) If multiple canaries show mismatch or artifact replication lag: pause rollout globally and open an incident channel.
5) If rollback required, use limited-scope rollback to canaries first, validate stability, then consider controlled promotion once fixed.
6) Run short decode validation on all canary hosts prior to resuming rollout.

Post-incident notes and open questions (work-in-progress):
- Should we tighten the roll-forward policy to require N consecutive successful decode round-trips before increasing traffic? Pros: reduces silent tokenization regressions. Cons: increases rollout time.
- What is acceptable replication lag threshold for critical artifacts (tokenizer/config) vs weights? Proposal: 30s for tokenizer, 2m for weights (needs infra input).
- How to surface artifact coupling in the UI/console so engineers can see mismatches pre-rollout?

Immediate action items (tracked in JIRA):
- JIRA-SRV-789: enforce artifact bundle atomicity (Ethan Zhao) - in progress.
- JIRA-SRV-790: preflight tokenizer hash validation (Marta Ruiz) - open.
- JIRA-SRV-791: add decode round-trip check to canary health probes (Daniel Kim) - planned.

Lessons learned (tl;dr):
- Decoupled artifacts + parallel streaming optimizations can create subtle races that only show up as decode errors.
- Health checks must include semantic checks (decode/encode round-trips), not just success/latency.
- Make artifact versioning explicit and visible in rollout UI.

Appendix (logs/snippets):
- Example error line: 2024-02-19T02:22:58Z ERROR decode: token-id 50212 not found in mapping (host=canary-5 shard=3)
- Example quick validation command: python -c "from tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer('/var/artifacts/tokenizer-vocab-20240218'); assert t.decode(t.encode('hello world')) == 'hello world'"

Notes to self / operator tips:
- If you must rollback weights while artifacts re-sync, prefer scoped rollback to canaries vs full fleet to reduce blast radius.
- Use redwoodctl artifact inspect --meta to compare expected vocab-sha256 from model manifest vs host artifact.

References / links:
- CONFLUENCE-ModelRollout-Notes (linked_artifacts)
- PR#4567 (rollback orchestration small fix)
- INC-2024-0421 (incident ticket)

Status: doc is draft-in-review; will convert to final post-action completion and attach final postmortem in Confluence.

Unresolved: need infra confirmation on object-store replication SLA and whether we can get push notifications on successful regional cache pulls.

-- Aisha
